caption: The vending machine number broke me a little. What is yours, honestly?

slides.title:
How I spend
my R14 800
p/m salary
Living in Gqeberha
slides.body:
Female, 26
Single, no kids, lives alone
Job: Call centre agent
Net salary: R14 800 p/m

slides.title: Rent
slides.includes: Bachelor flat in Newton Park, water and refuse
slides.body: It is one room. It is ten minutes from the office and that is the whole point.

slides.title: Groceries
slides.includes: Shoprite, and the mid-month top-ups I do not plan for
slides.body: I cook for one and still throw food away. I have not figured that out yet.

slides.title: Personal loan
slides.includes: R18 000 taken out when my mom's fridge and my laptop went in the same month
slides.body: Fourteen months left. The interest on it is the number I actively avoid looking at.

slides.title: Money home
slides.includes: My mom's electricity, my brother's school shoes and transport
slides.body: She never asks. I send it anyway because I know what the month looks like there.

slides.title: Takeaways & vending machine
slides.includes: Night shift snacks, Friday KFC, the office machine
slides.body: I said R400. I checked. It was R1 150. Most of it is R18 at a time on a bad shift.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: Taxi fare, electricity, airtime & data, clothing account, funeral policy, stokvel, hair & nails, savings
slides.body: R4 380 of small things. On R14 800 the small things are the whole problem.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R14 800. That is R27 a day, and payday is never as close as I think it is.

slides.title: I stopped guessing
slides.body:
I uploaded three months of statements to Beyond Horizon and it sorted every transaction for me.

The R18 vending machine taps added up to more than my electricity.

No bank login needed.
